keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 25-29; no Cliopatria row. The Guangwu page: Peng Chong 'claimed the title of the Prince of Yan and controlled the modern Beijing region'. The page gives no frontier; the Beijing municipality stands for it, with the Han commanderies of Yuyang and Shanggu round it unmapped.

ledger.note: 25: Peng Chong holds the Beijing region, bridged. The page lists him among the rival powers after Liu Xiu's accession (summer 25) but dates neither his rise nor his title of Prince of Yan. PAGE SILENT. [Reviewer ea-02-x, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from lulin (dossier ends 23) to han-dynasty, which carries the Gengshi and Eastern Han regime]

ledger.note: 29: Peng Chong is killed. 'Also in AD 29, Peng's slaves assassinated him, leading to a collapse of his regime.'

ledger.note: 29: Yan ends with Peng Chong's assassination; the Beijing region passes to the Eastern Han.

certainty.note: Only the modern municipality is named.

sources.title: Emperor Guangwu of Han
sources.note: The rival regional powers of AD 25-36: who controlled which modern region; dates of their fall.

notes: Peng Chong, Yan 25-29. 1 page opened (Emperor Guangwu of Han); the English Wikipedia 'Peng Chong' is a different man (a CCP official) and 'Yan Kingdom (Han dynasty)' does not mention him; no article of his own found. Cliopatria has no row. Unsettled: start year (confidence 1), the capital (Ji is the Han Yan capital, not named for him on any page), the commanderies he held, his alliances.
